newsitem.title: VIETNAM: SOCCER-PITCH VIOLENCE SHAMES VIETNAM POLICE AGAIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PITCH VIOLENCE SHAMES VIETNAM POLICE AGAIN.

text.p: Two players from the Hanoi Police soccer team have been suspended for kicking and punching opponents in an ill-tempered match against the army side earlier this week, the Vietnam Football Federation said on Friday.
The Federation said in a statement that Nguyen Duc Thinh had been banned for two league matches and Mai Tien Dung for four matches.

Wednesday's ill-tempered match, which follows an attack by Ho Chi Minh City Police players on a referee last October, has raised concern about growing violence on the country's soccer pitches. One of the national side's top stars was banned from the game for life for leading that assualt.

Although the football fraternity has been shaken by the incident, there was more concern among fans this week that the national team's much-admired coach, Karl Weigang, may be about to sign a contract with Malaysian premier league club Perak.
The daily Vietnam News quoted Weigang -- a German who made his name as coach for the national team of former South Vietnam in the 1960s -- as saying that he had not signed anything yet.

"On my way to Germany I had stopovers in Malaysia and in Singapore and I had discussions with club officials offering me new contracts," he was reported as saying in an open letter from Germany. "The fact is that I have not signed any contract."
